themes_detail.label: Graffiti surge in Morris Park
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 17 THIS WEEK, up 807% from the 8-week average of 1.9 complaints per week (z-score: 4.82), suggesting a sudden coordinated tagging campaign or breakdown in enforcement across the district.
evidence: 17 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
807% spike with z-score of 4.82 (statistically significant anomaly)
No prior recent surge in graffiti complaints in 90-day dataset
reporting_angles: Document graffiti hotspots by mapping 17 complaints; interview residents about visibility and timeline
Contact NYPD and Parks Dept. about any known tagging crews or anti-graffiti operations in progress

themes_detail.label: Drug activity spike this week
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints jumped to 15 THIS WEEK, up 991% from the 8-week baseline of 1.4 per week (z-score: 7.05, highest severity rating), marking the most extreme statistical anomaly in the dataset and suggesting either a new open-air market or sudden enforcement action.
evidence: 15 drug activity complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
991% increase with z-score of 7.05 (highest severity spike in entire dataset)
Community board budget repeatedly requests additional police officers, suggesting ongoing public safety concerns
reporting_angles: Investigate whether complaints cluster geographically (specific blocks/parks); interview residents about visibility and safety concerns
Request NYPD data on arrests, undercover operations, or known dealers in Morris Park this week; ask if enforcement uptick triggered complaints surge

themes_detail.label: Street infrastructure damage
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK, up 433% from the 8-week average of 1.1 per week (z-score: 4.63), alongside a separate spike in obstruction complaints 2 weeks ago (10 vs. 2.9 avg), suggesting possible weather event, vehicle collisions, or infrastructure decay.
evidence: 6 street sign damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Obstruction complaints spiked to 10 two weeks ago (248% above 2.9 avg), suggesting possible related pattern of infrastructure disruption
reporting_angles: Canvas Morris Park and Pelham Parkway neighborhoods to document damaged signs; photograph locations and assess cause (weather, vehicle impact, decay)
File FOIL for DOT work orders on street sign repairs this month; ask if spike correlates with recent weather, construction, or accidents

themes_detail.label: Rodent infestation uptick
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints rose to 11 LAST WEEK, up 175% from the 8-week average of 4.0 per week (z-score: 4.67), aligning with community board's repeated requests for DEP catch basin cleaning and suggesting inadequate sanitation infrastructure.
evidence: 11 rodent complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Community board budget submitted repeated 'clean catch basins' requests to DEP, indicating systemic drainage/sanitation issue
reporting_angles: Interview residents with rodent complaints to establish whether infestation is in homes, streets, or parks; ask when they first noticed increase
Request DEP data on catch basin cleaning schedules and recent work in Morris Park/Pelham Parkway; ask if infrastructure backlog is contributing to rodent habitat

themes_detail.label: Unleashed dog complaints surge
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints hit 3 LAST WEEK, up 500% from the 8-week average of 0.5 per week (z-score: 5.0), suggesting either a new population of stray or unsupervised dogs or increased community reporting of an existing problem.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Community board budget requests enhanced park safety, including potential dog-related concerns
reporting_angles: Identify which parks or blocks saw unleashed dog complaints; interview residents and dog owners about problem visibility and frequency
Contact Parks Enforcement and NYPD about enforcement actions and whether stray dog population has grown
